definition: Finding the start and end times of action instances within untrimmed video and classifying them.
details: Finding the start and end times of action instances within untrimmed video and classifying them. It combines detection and recognition over time for surveillance and sports analytics.

explainer.lead: Temporal action localization finds the start and end times of action instances within untrimmed video and classifies them. It matters because it combines detection and recognition over time, which surveillance and sports analytics depend on.

tiers.eli5: Given a long video, it marks where each action begins and ends and says what the action is.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to untrimmed footage where the action is not already clipped, needing both boundaries and class labels. The available facts give no architecture or evaluation details beyond its use in surveillance and sports analytics.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally the task of predicting start and end times plus a class for each action instance in untrimmed video; it combines detection and recognition over time. Its stated application areas are surveillance and sports analytics.

explainer.example: In an untrimmed surveillance recording, the system reports that a person falls from timestamp A to timestamp B and labels the segment as a fall.
